label: Bamako
sub: Mali's capital and seat of the Goïta junta. Site of 2020 and 2021 coups; Africa Corps HQ. Day 34 (June 1) of JNIM 'total siege' declared April 28, 2026. Post-Eid window (May 28–June 5) ongoing with no new JNIM major escalation. March 2026 fuel truce expired; US Embassy Enhanced Security Alert expired May 31 without renewal. 3 of 6 supply corridors cut; food prices +43–65%; WFP suspended ($620M gap); IRC emergency active. IRC one-month assessment (June 1): 5.1M Malians need aid, 1.5M at crisis hunger. FAO projects 52.8M at IPC Phase 3+ in June–August lean season. Goïta reshuffled theater commands May 29–30.

label: Ouagadougou
sub: Burkina Faso's capital; site of two coups in 2022. Ibrahim Traoré's junta HQ. Africa Corps troops present. ~40% of national territory estimated outside government control.

label: Niamey
sub: Niger's capital; site of July 2023 coup by Gen. Tchiani. Former Operation Barkhane sub-HQ. US forces expelled April–August 2024. Russian military advisers now present.

label: Gao
sub: Former MUJAO stronghold liberated January 2013. Major French Barkhane base (Camp Firgun). Now the Africa Corps/FAMa operational hub for northern Mali. Starting point of the 2023 Kidal offensive column.

label: Kidal
sub: Former Tuareg/MNLA stronghold. Secured by French forces January 30, 2013. Fell to CSP-PSD rebels 2014–2023. Recaptured by FAMa/Africa Corps November 14, 2023. April 25–26, 2026: FLA forces seized the city during the nationwide JNIM-FLA offensive. Africa Corps and FAMa withdrew under FLA escort on April 26 — Kidal declared 'totally' under FLA control. Largest territorial loss for the Mali junta-Russia axis since Africa Corps deployed in 2021.

label: Timbuktu
sub: Ancient city liberated from jihadists January 27, 2013. Under JNIM blockade since 2024; supply lines cut. Russian Africa Corps airbase struck by JNIM June 2, 2025; 60+ FAMa killed.

label: Bagare
sub: VDP post in Passor province, northern Burkina Faso. Site of JNIM motorcycle assault May 1–2, 2026 that killed at least 11 VDP volunteers. Shops and vehicles burned. JNIM claimed seizure of 'military post belonging to the Burkinabe militias.'

label: Mopti
sub: Epicenter of Katiba Macina / Fulani jihad. Amadou Koufa's home region. First zone of Wagner deployment (December 2021). Hub for Dogon-Fulani inter-communal violence. Near the Moura massacre site.

label: Ménaka
sub: IS-Sahel / ISGS operational heartland. Controls Gao-Ménaka corridor and access to the Liptako-Gourma tri-border zone. Sustained ISGS-FAMa fighting since 2017. April 28, 2026: ISSP seized the urban area of Ménaka; Malian Army and Africa Corps retreated into the fortified former UN camp west of the city. IS fighters occupied the local administration building and set up checkpoints. City split — ISSP holds urban core, government forces hold the base.

label: Tessalit
sub: Former French/US drone and intelligence base near the Algerian border. Former MINUSMA camp now occupied by FAMa and Africa Corps.

label: Konna
sub: Site of the January 10, 2013 jihadist advance that triggered Operation Serval. Amadou Koufa briefly declared 'Sultan of Konna.' Retaken by FAMa/French January 17, 2013.

label: Sévaré
sub: Key airfield 70 km south of Konna; the only military-capable airport outside Bamako. JNIM's capture of Konna in January 2013 put Sévaré within striking distance, triggering France's emergency intervention.

label: Diabaly
sub: Second jihadist axis of advance in January 2013. MUJAO forces captured Diabaly before being halted by French airstrikes. Its fall threatened the strategic Ségou-Bamako corridor.

label: Moura
sub: Site of the March 27–31, 2022 Moura massacre. FAMa and Wagner forces killed at least 500 civilians according to UN OHCHR. The single worst atrocity of the Sahel conflict. Malian junta blocked investigation.

label: Aguelhok
sub: Site of January 24, 2012 massacre of ~82 Malian soldiers by MNLA and Ansar Dine. Former MINUSMA camp. FAMa/Africa Corps base targeted by FLA FPV kamikaze drone strikes in March–April 2026. April 27, 2026: Africa Corps officially confirmed withdrawal from Aguelhok as part of full repositioning from the Kidal Region to Anéfis following the fall of Kidal on April 26.

label: Kati Garrison
sub: Mali's largest military garrison, 15 km from Bamako. Home of junta leader Gen. Assimi Goïta. Site of the March 2012 mutiny (Sanogo coup) and the September 2024 JNIM VBIED attack. April 25, 2026: JNIM launched a major pre-dawn assault with explosions and sustained gunfire; Defense Minister Sadio Camara's residence at Kati was attacked/destroyed. Largest attack on Bamako-area military infrastructure in the conflict.

label: Ogossagou
sub: Fulani village in Mopti Region. Site of March 23, 2019 Ogossagou massacre — ~160 Fulani civilians killed by Dogon hunters' militia (Dan Nan Ambassagou). Worst inter-communal atrocity in modern Malian history.

label: Tongo Tongo
sub: Village in Niger's Tillabéri Region. Site of October 4, 2017 ISGS ambush that killed 4 US Special Forces soldiers and 4 Nigerien troops — the largest US combat loss in Africa since Somalia 1993.

label: Inates
sub: Nigerien military camp in Tillabéri Region. Site of December 10, 2019 ISGS assault killing 71 soldiers — the deadliest single attack in Niger's military history. Prompted ECOWAS emergency summit.

label: Tillabéri Region
sub: Northwestern Niger; IS-Sahel / ISGS operational heartland. Borders the Liptako-Gourma tri-border zone. Sustained attacks on military bases 2017–present. US Air Base 101 in nearby Niamey provided drone coverage until 2024.

label: Liptako-Gourma (Tri-Border)
sub: Mali-Niger-Burkina Faso border zone. Historical ISGS stronghold and most violent area of the Sahel conflict. Hundreds of attacks annually; estimated thousands of civilians killed 2017–2024.

label: Djibo
sub: Provincial capital in Burkina Faso's Sahel Region. Under JNIM blockade since 2022; resupply only by air. May 11, 2026: JNIM overran the town in a 9-hour occupation (5AM–2PM), killing 100+ civilians, soldiers, and VDP volunteers. Military base seized, gendarmerie HQ, police HQ, hospital, and market attacked and looted. JNIM posted videos of captured weapons. Largest single JNIM operation in Burkina Faso history.

label: Dori
sub: Capital of Burkina Faso's Sahel Region. Hub of JNIM activity in northeastern Burkina. Periodic blockades and road ambushes have isolated surrounding communities.

label: Kaya
sub: Key logistics hub in Burkina Faso's Centre-Nord Region. JNIM convoy ambushes on the Ouagadougou-Kaya-Dori road have blocked humanitarian and military resupply to the north since 2022.

label: Fada N'Gourma
sub: Capital of Burkina Faso's Est Region. Gateway to the W National Park zone and the JNIM/IS-Sahel operational corridor toward Benin, Togo, and Ghana.

label: Pama (W Park Area)
sub: Southern Burkina Faso near the W National Park. JNIM/IS-Sahel operating zone for attacks into northern Benin. A Benin military convoy was ambushed here, killing 54 soldiers in 2025.

label: Porga (Benin)
sub: Town in Atacora Department, northern Benin, ~30 km from Burkina Faso border. May 7, 2026: JNIM fighters attacked the military post, killing 7 Beninese soldiers and seizing weapons and motorcycles. Represents JNIM's confirmed operational reach into a Gulf of Guinea coastal state — part of the documented southward expansion corridor from Burkina Faso's Est Region through the W-Arly-Pendjari (WAP) park complex.

label: Boulkessi
sub: Malian military base near the Burkina Faso border. JNIM assault June 1, 2025: 60+ FAMa killed, ~220 taken hostage, weapons and vehicles seized. Among the heaviest single-day Malian military losses.

label: Douentza
sub: Town in Mopti Region. Captured by MUJAO in September 2012, retaken by French/Malian forces in 2013. Remains a contested corridor between Mopti and Gao.

label: Gourma-Rharous
sub: Timbuktu Region cercle. Major JNIM activity zone along the Niger River corridor. Site of multiple JNIM operations blocking Timbuktu resupply since 2023.

label: Ansongo
sub: Gao Region town on the Mali-Niger border. Contested JNIM/IS-Sahel zone. Bridge crossing for fighters between Mali and Niger. Multiple FAMa convoy ambushes 2019–2024.

label: Hombori
sub: Gao Region village. Site of July 2023 HRW-documented atrocities by Malian army and apparent Wagner fighters. New pattern of civilian killings emerged in surrounding area 2023.

label: Gossi
sub: Former French Barkhane base in the Gourma Region. MINUSMA camp also present. Site of documented Wagner Group incident in April 2022 when Russia staged fake 'mass grave' propaganda after French withdrawal.

label: Anéfis
sub: Staging point for the October–November 2023 FAMa/Wagner offensive toward Kidal. CSP-PSD Tuareg rebels held this town temporarily before the Wagner advance. FAMa/Africa Corps compound at Anéfis struck by FLA (Front de Libération de l'Azawad) drone and missile attack March 30, 2026 — the seventh FLA operation claimed in March 2026.

label: Ber
sub: Village near Timbuktu on the JNIM supply-interdiction corridor. Site of repeated FAMa convoy ambushes as JNIM tightened the Timbuktu siege 2023–2024.

label: Ségou
sub: Fourth-largest Malian city. Ségou Region is a major JNIM expansion zone, linking Katiba Macina operations in Mopti to growing activity in western Mali toward Senegal and Mauritania.

label: Nara
sub: Mali-Mauritania border area. JNIM expanding westward into Kayes and Nara regions since 2023. Multiple attacks on gendarmerie posts and convoys. Threatens Mauritanian border security.

label: Niafunké
sub: Timbuktu Region town. Birthplace of Amadou Koufa (from nearby Saraféré). Fulani pastoral recruitment heartland for Katiba Macina. Suffered repeated JNIM-aligned blockades of market access.

label: Ouahigouya
sub: Capital of Burkina Faso's Nord Region. JNIM expansion zone in northern Burkina Faso. Supply routes to surrounding villages repeatedly ambushed; surrounding schools closed.

label: Titao
sub: Loroum Province, Burkina Faso. JNIM and IS-Sahel activities in this corridor connecting the Sahel and Nord regions. Multiple VDP and FAB ambushes 2021–2024.

label: Ouallam
sub: Tillabéri Region, Niger. IS-Sahel attack corridor toward Niamey. Multiple military base attacks and civilian massacres in surrounding area 2019–2024.

label: Diffa
sub: Niger's southeast region. Secondary threat zone — Boko Haram / ISWAP activities from Lake Chad basin, overlapping with IS-Sahel expansion eastward.

label: Agadez
sub: Niger's major northern city. Site of US Air Base 201 — a $110M drone and intelligence facility from which Reaper drones tracked JNIM and ISGS leadership. US completed withdrawal August 2024.

label: Tahoua
sub: Central Niger region experiencing spillover IS-Sahel violence from Tillabéri. IS-Sahel expansion corridor toward Tahoua documented by ACLED from 2021.

label: Téra
sub: Tillabéri Region town on the Mali-Niger border. ISGS / IS-Sahel activity zone. Site of December 2021 attack on security force and civilians during an AU democracy march (69+ killed).

label: N'Djamena
sub: Capital of Chad; Operation Barkhane's permanent headquarters 2014–2022. French forces still present (reduced to ~1,000). Hub for remaining French regional operations in Africa.

label: Africa Corps Compound (Bamako)
sub: Russia's Africa Corps (formerly Wagner) permanent compound in Bamako. Satellite imagery confirms expanded facilities. Main coordination base for ~1,000-1,500 Africa Corps personnel in Mali.

label: Bobo-Dioulasso
sub: Burkina Faso's second city; economic hub. JNIM expansion threatening approaches to Bobo-Dioulasso from the north and west. Multiple attacks on surrounding villages 2022–2024.

label: Kongoussi
sub: Centre-Nord Region, Burkina Faso. JNIM attacks on gendarmerie and villages in Kongoussi area; gateway town on the deteriorating Kaya-Dori security corridor.

label: Pô
sub: Southern Burkina Faso near Ghana border. JNIM expansion southward threatening the Ghana and Togo borders. Attacks on gendarmerie posts 2023–2024.

label: Macina
sub: Historical name for central Mali; birthplace of the 19th-century Fulani Macina Empire that Amadou Koufa invokes as ideological justification for Katiba Macina. JNIM expansion corridor from Ségou to Mopti.

label: Bankass
sub: Mopti Region cercle near the Dogon Country and Burkina Faso border. Intense JNIM/Katiba Macina activity; multiple attacks on security posts 2018–2024.

label: Djenné
sub: Ancient UNESCO World Heritage city in Mopti Region; cercle encompassing the Moura massacre site. JNIM controls surrounding rural areas; Djenné itself has been under threat since 2018.

label: Bourem
sub: Gao Region town on the Niger River. JNIM and IS-Sahel both active in Bourem cercle. Transit corridor for armed groups between Gao and Kidal regions.

label: Tenenkou
sub: Mopti Region cercle. Core Katiba Macina territory; Fulani pastoral community stronghold for JNIM recruitment. Multiple attacks on security forces 2016–2024.

label: Nampala
sub: Ségou Region border town near Mauritania. JNIM base camp area. Malian military base at Nampala repeatedly attacked 2016–2020; 25+ soldiers killed in single 2016 attack.

label: Nioro du Sahel
sub: Kayes Region town near the Mauritanian border. JNIM westward expansion front. Attacks on gendarmerie and civilians increased 2023–2025 as JNIM expanded toward Senegal.

label: Mondoro
sub: Mopti Region near Burkina Faso border. Major JNIM transit and logistics base for cross-border operations between central Mali and northern Burkina Faso.

label: MINUSMA HQ (Former)
sub: MINUSMA headquarters in Bamako. Mission operated July 2013–December 2023. Largest UN peacekeeping mission budget in history (~$1.2B/year). 304 total deaths including 175 from hostile acts.

label: Splendid Hotel Attack Site
sub: Central Ouagadougou. Site of January 15, 2016 AQIM/al-Mourabitoun attack killing 30 people — Burkina Faso's worst terrorist atrocity at the time and signal of jihadist southward expansion.

label: Radisson Blu Attack Site
sub: Bamako. Site of November 20, 2015 AQIM/al-Mourabitoun hotel siege killing 22 people including diplomats and UN staff. Demonstrated jihadist ability to strike the capital.

label: Diré
sub: Timbuktu Region town on the Niger River. JNIM transit corridor between Timbuktu and western Mali. Supply route interdiction operations cut off Diré from 2023.

label: Nondin / Soro
sub: Villages in Burkina Faso, Sissili Province. Site of February 25, 2024 massacre of 223 civilians (including 56 children) by Burkinabè forces and VDP militias — called potential crimes against humanity by HRW.

label: Camp Firgun (Former Barkhane Base)
sub: France's main operational base for Operation Barkhane in Mali, at Gao airport. Transferred to MINUSMA and FAMa following France's 2022 withdrawal. Now used by FAMa and Africa Corps.

label: Taoudenni
sub: Remote northern Mali region with significant gold deposits. FAMa and Africa Corps extending control northward after Kidal capture. Previously inaccessible state authority zone.

label: Ménaka (IS-Sahel Stronghold)
sub: IS-Sahel province administrative center. Adnan Abu Walid al-Sahrawi's primary operational zone before his 2021 killing. Massive civilian displacement from IS-Sahel ethnic targeting campaigns 2019–2022.

label: Faramana
sub: Burkina Faso-Mali border crossing. JNIM use this corridor to coordinate operations between central Mali and western Burkina Faso. Customs post repeatedly attacked 2022–2024.

label: Bourzanga
sub: Bam Province, Burkina Faso. Site of a January 2023 VDP convoy massacre by JNIM — among the worst single-incident civilian losses in Burkina Faso.

label: Léré
sub: Tombouctou Region town on the Mauritanian border. Site of early MNLA attacks January 2012. Targeted by French airstrikes in the first hours of Operation Serval January 11, 2013.

label: Sokolo
sub: Ségou Region, Mali. JNIM attacks on Sokolo gendarmerie multiple times 2019–2023. Major Katiba Macina recruitment and attack corridor between Mopti and Ségou regions.

label: Bagade
sub: Northern Burkina Faso (Soum/Loroum area). Site of March 22, 2026 JNIM assault on military post killing at least 14 soldiers. Part of JNIM's ongoing offensive campaign of 30+ attacks in Burkina Faso since February 2026.

label: Sanama
sub: Tillabéri Region, Niger. IS-Sahel attack on Niger Army positions March 25, 2026 killed 6 soldiers. Part of ongoing IS-Sahel pressure on military positions in western Niger.

label: Tonka
sub: Timbuktu Region municipality on the Niger River. JNIM assassination of youth association deputy president Amadou Baby ('Marco') on March 27, 2026 — part of JNIM's campaign of targeted killings against civil society figures perceived as collaborating with security forces.

label: Arbinda
sub: Commune in Soum Province, Burkina Faso's Sahel Region. Site of major FAB air-ground counterinsurgency operation on April 13–14, 2026, in which approximately 100 jihadist fighters were killed northeast of the town — among the largest single-operation claimed successes of the FAB in 2026.

label: Nakamba Sector
sub: East-central Burkina Faso (Centre-Est/Est region corridor). FAB eliminated JNIM field commander/emir Karim Torodo (alias Abdul Bashir, age 35) in this sector in mid-April 2026 — a commander who had a 175 million CFA franc bounty since June 2023. JNIM's Centre-Est operational zone connecting northern Burkina Faso networks to the southeastern expansion corridor toward Benin and Togo.

label: Ayorou
sub: Tillabéri Region, Niger — on the Niger River at the Mali-Niger border confluence. Niger National Guard camp attacked by armed militants on April 19, 2026; 3 soldiers killed. Strategically located crossing point for armed group movements between Mali and Niger's Tillabéri corridor.

label: Tessit
sub: Ansongo Department, Gao Region, Mali — near Mali-Niger border. IS-Sahel (ISGS) recurring attack site; deadliest incident: August 7–8, 2022 assault killed 42 soldiers. IS-Sahel attacked again April 23, 2026; FAMa repelled. April 27, 2026: JNIM captured Tessit after the Malian army agreed to surrender their weapons in exchange for safe passage — another negotiated capitulation following the fall of Kidal two days earlier.

label: Dioura (FAMa Strike Area)
sub: Mopti Region, Mali — JNIM Katiba Macina operational zone. FAMa conducted precision airstrikes northwest of Dioura on April 23, 2026, destroying a major terrorist base and neutralizing 60+ militants. Dioura and its cercle have been subject to repeated JNIM attacks on military and gendarmerie posts since 2016.

label: Labbezanga
sub: Mali-Niger border fort at the Niger River crossing — a key transit point between northeastern Mali (Gao Region) and Niger's Tillabéri Region. April 27, 2026: ISSP (Islamic State – Sahel Province) seized the Labbezanga border fort after Malian troops abandoned the post and fled toward Ansongo. Niger closed its Mali border crossing in response. June 1, 2026: FAMa and Africa Corps claimed to have recaptured Labbezanga (Pravda Mali — single Russian-aligned source, not independently confirmed as of June 2). If confirmed, would mark the first reversal of an April 2026 ISSP territorial gain.

label: Kenieroba Prison
sub: Kenieroba Central Prison — Mali's maximum-security facility 60km southwest of Bamako, dubbed 'Africa's Alcatraz.' Houses 2,500 inmates including at least 72 high-value detainees (JNIM fighters and April 2026 offensive suspects). Attacked by JNIM fighters on May 6–7, 2026 as part of the ongoing Bamako siege; FAMa repelled the assault. Simultaneous supply-convoy arson and blockade checkpoints reinstated around Bamako during the attack.

label: Korikori/Gomossogou
sub: Villages in Mopti Region, central Mali. Site of JNIM twin village massacres on the night of May 6–7, 2026 (reported May 8). JNIM simultaneously raided Korikori and Gomossagou, opening fire and torching properties — killing at least 30–50+ villagers. JNIM cited the Dan Na Ambassagou (DNA) self-defense militia's cooperation with FAMa as justification, consistent with JNIM's campaign of reprisals against Mopti-area communities perceived as supporting state counter-insurgency. FAMa conducted a follow-up counter-operation killing approximately 12 JNIM fighters.

label: Diapaga
sub: Capital of Tapoa Province, Est Region, Burkina Faso — approximately 25 km from the Togolese border. May 12–13, 2026: JNIM overran the army outpost, killing 50+ soldiers and VDP auxiliaries, destroying buildings and monuments, releasing prisoners (including suspected jihadists), and seizing weapons before withdrawing. The last major FAB buffer post before the Togo border; its fall threatens the Lomé–Fada N'Gourma–Ouagadougou commercial corridor and places Togolese border towns (Tambi, Mango, Dapaong) at direct risk. Part of JNIM's coordinated southeastern expansion: Djibo (May 11) → Diapaga (May 13) — demonstrating multi-regional simultaneous strike capacity.

label: Manantali Dam (JNIM Infrastructure Target)
sub: Manantali hydroelectric dam on the Bafing River, Kayes Region, Mali — primary electricity source for Bamako. May 12, 2026: JNIM sabotaged the Manantali transmission line as part of the ongoing Bamako siege, threatening hospital operations, water supply, banking, and telecommunications. The attack escalated JNIM's infrastructure warfare from road/supply interdiction to direct grid sabotage — part of a pattern of siege-by-infrastructure alongside prison assault (May 6–7), convoy arson, and checkpoint blockades.

label: Diabou (JNIM Attack Site)
sub: Town in Gourma Province, Est Region, Burkina Faso. May 14, 2026: ~300 JNIM militants attacked Diabou, killing at least 2 civilians, looting and destroying farm plots, and seizing dozens of cattle. Multiple surrounding villages have been encircled by JNIM fighters forcing residents to flee. Part of JNIM's sustained eastern Burkina Faso offensive arc: Djibo (May 11) → Diapaga (May 12–13) → Diabou (May 14). Gourma Province borders Niger and is a key corridor for JNIM's eastward and southward expansion toward the Gulf of Guinea.

label: Diafarabé (Massacre Site)
sub: Town in Tenenkou Cercle, Mopti Region, Mali, on the Niger River. May 12, 2026: Malian soldiers and Dozo militia arrested at least 30 Fulani men at the local cattle market, bound and blindfolded them, transported them by canoe across the Niger River, and executed them. May 15, 2026: Residents discovered 22 bodies in two mass graves on the south bank of the Niger River; victims were Fulani men aged 32–67. Amnesty International and FIDH called for urgent independent investigation. Pattern consistent with documented Fulani collective punishment operations in the Mopti-Ségou corridor (Moura 2022, Ogossagou 2019). Junta has not issued a response.

label: Mbera/Doueinkara (Malian Refugee Zone)
sub: Hodh Chargui Region, eastern Mauritania. UNHCR Mbera camp and MSF Doueinkara healthcare centre — primary reception zone for ~300,000 Malian refugees (170,000+ registered Malians). May 19–21, 2026: MSF coordinator documented systematic torture, sexual violence, being burned alive and beheaded, and massacres among refugees who fled FAMa and Africa Corps operations in northern Mali. AFP photojournalists accompanied MSF teams in May 2026. FIDH/TRIAL International/PALU filed a landmark case before the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights on April 20, 2026 seeking accountability for atrocities by Mali's security forces and Africa Corps.

label: Tene (FAMa Drone Strike Site)
sub: Village in San District, Ségou Region, central Mali. May 18, 2026: FAMa drones struck a motorbike procession of villagers gathering for a traditional collective wedding ceremony, killing at least 10 civilians including children. A security source told AFP the drones targeted 'a procession of motorbikes following one another' that drew military attention. Multiple outlets confirmed via AFP wire. Malian junta has not issued a statement. Represents a documented pattern of FAMa drone targeting of civilian motorcycle movements in central Mali.

label: Goubré IDP Camp
sub: Centre-Nord Region, Burkina Faso. An internally displaced persons camp housing ~3,500 people who had already fled earlier JNIM violence. May 22, 2026: JNIM attacked the camp, killing 80 people including 72 civilians (45 men, 23 women, 2 girls, 2 boys) and 8 VDP fighters. JNIM claimed responsibility on May 24, citing VDP presence; UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Burkina Faso condemned the attack and noted an aid worker was killed. Camp closed following the massacre. One of the most severe single JNIM atrocities against displaced civilians in the Sahel crisis.

label: Tadjmart/Aguelhoc (Cluster Bomb Site)
sub: Hamlet near Aguelhoc, Kidal Region, northern Mali. May 16-17, 2026: Africa Corps/FAMa aircraft dropped what RFI weapons specialist identified as a Russian-made RBK-500 cluster bomb delivery system, scattering ShOAB-0.5 submunitions across the area. One child was killed and three women injured. A second cluster bomb strike occurred near Oubder (In-Gouzma, Timbuktu Region). Story broke May 23. Africa Corps and Mali are non-signatories to the Convention on Cluster Munitions. FLA condemned the strikes and collected unexploded submunitions as evidence for accountability proceedings.

label: Titao (Loroum Convoy Attack)
sub: Capital of Loroum Province, Nord Region, Burkina Faso. May 29, 2026: JNIM militants on motorcycles attacked a trading convoy on the Titao-Sollé axis killing at least 15 civilians including women and children. Consistent with JNIM's sustained pressure on commercial supply routes throughout northern Burkina Faso's provincial towns.

label: Barsalogho (ICRC Convoy Attack)
sub: Sanmatenga Province, Centre-Nord Region, Burkina Faso. May 29–30, 2026: JNIM ambushed an aid convoy (escorted by gendarmes) returning from the Foube refugee camp near Barsalogho. At least 13 killed (5 gendarmes + 5+ civilians including an ICRC ambulance driver and nurse), 40 wounded, 6 gendarmes missing. A grave breach of IHL targeting ICRC-protected humanitarian personnel.

label: Kompienbiga (Market Massacre)
sub: Kompienga Province, Est Region, Burkina Faso, ~60 km south of Diapaga. May 31, 2026: Gunmen on motorcycles burst into the livestock market during Eid al-Adha, killing approximately 30 civilians before fleeing. Security source attributed the attack to 'armed groups with links to al-Qaeda and Daesh.' Comes 18 days after JNIM seized Diapaga (May 13) and 9 days after the Goubré IDP camp massacre (May 22). Demonstrates JNIM's sustained multi-district operational tempo across the Est Region.

label: Bamako–Kayes Highway (IED Strike)
sub: Kita area, Kayes Region, western Mali. June 1, 2026: A passenger bus struck a JNIM-planted landmine on the Bamako–Kayes highway, killing 8 and injuring 42. The western supply artery connecting Bamako to Senegal, Mauritania, and Guinea — one of the last partially functional corridors during the JNIM siege. ISS Africa (June 4, 2026) identifies this route as part of JNIM's systematic 'strategy of asphyxiation' targeting the Dakar-Bamako trade corridor, costing $26.5M/month to Senegal's port alone.

label: Koumbri (Military Base Attack)
sub: Yatenga Province, Nord Region, Burkina Faso. June 1, 2026: JNIM fighters overran the military base at Koumbri, killing 45 Burkinabè soldiers and 10 VDP (Volunteers for the Defense of the Motherland) — one of the deadliest single-day FAB tolls of the conflict. Comes at the end of what was already the deadliest month in Burkina Faso's insurgency history (May 2026, ~300+ killed in five major atrocities). Source: Crisis Group CrisisWatch / Islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso timeline — independent verification limited. Contested.

label: Anéfis (Battle for Anéfis)
sub: Kidal Region, Mali. Jul 4–10, 2026: FLA-JNIM coalition seized most of the town in a coordinated offensive; government forces claimed recapture around Jul 8–10 after an airstrike campaign and ground counteroffensive. A key waypoint on the Kidal-Bourem-Gao supply route. Fighting continued around the town through mid-July, including an ambush of a departing convoy near Tabankort on Jul 17-18.

label: Tabrichat (Relief Convoy Ambush)
sub: Gao–Kidal corridor, Mali. Jul 5–9, 2026: FLA-JNIM forces twice ambushed Africa Corps relief/resupply convoys headed toward besieged Anéfis, downing a Mi-24 helicopter (Jul 5) and IED-ambushing a ~67-vehicle resupply column (Jul 7–9). Single tier-3 source; confidence low.

label: Tabankort (Convoy Ambush)
sub: Gao region, Mali, on the Anéfis–Gao road. Jul 17–18, 2026: FLA-JNIM forces ambushed a FAMa/Africa Corps convoy departing recaptured Anéfis. Casualties disputed — aggregated reporting cites ~50 soldiers killed and 20 captured; Mali's military did not confirm specific numbers.

label: Inafarak (First Shahed-136-Type Strike)
sub: Timbuktu Region, Mali. Jul 12, 2026: First confirmed use of a Shahed-136-type/Garpiya-A1 loitering munition on the Mali battlefield, geolocated by open-source researchers. No casualty figures reported. Single-source (Rio Times); confidence low.

label: Talahandak (Second Shahed-136-Type Strike)
sub: Northern Mali. Jul 17, 2026: Second confirmed Shahed-136-type/Garpiya-A1 loitering munition strike. No casualty figures reported. Single-source (Rio Times); confidence low.

label: Abeibara (Africa Corps Interdiction Ops)
sub: Kidal Region, Mali. Aug 3–4, 2026: FAMa/Africa Corps 'Operation Dougoukoloko' reportedly detected JNIM weapons stocks near Abeibara and destroyed JNIM logistics infrastructure in Kidal city. Single Russian-state-linked source (African Initiative); unverified, confidence low.

label: San (Barracks Assault)
sub: Ségou Region, Mali. Aug 9, 2026: JNIM fighters attacked and temporarily occupied FAMa's main barracks in San — well south of the historical northern front, closer to Bamako's approaches. At least 10 soldiers killed (AFP); Mali's military claims ~40 militants killed in response (disputed).

label: Kyrnia (Africa Corps Airstrike — 8 Civilians Killed)
sub: Mopti Region, Mali. Jun 15, 2026 (reported by HRW Jul 31, 2026): An Africa Corps Su-24 dropped two munitions on Kyrnia village on a market day, killing 8 civilians including 3 children. HRW found ~100 JNIM fighters were present but concentrated ~150m from the actual impact sites, with no evidence of a military objective at the points struck.

label: Bankilaré–Téra Axis (Army Detachment Ambush)
sub: Tillabéri Region, Niger, near Doungouro village. Jul 17, 2026: Niger Armed Forces liaison detachment ambushed on contested ISSP/JNIM ground. Official toll: 16 killed, 23 wounded. Unofficial (RFI): 47+ killed. African Union condemned the attack Jul 18.

label: Dankassari (Military Base Overrun)
sub: Dosso Region, Niger, between Doutchi and Yaya. Jul 31, 2026: Suspected ISSP fighters overran a Nigerien forward operating base, killing 21 soldiers.

label: N'Guigmi (Military Post Attack)
sub: Diffa Region, Niger, near Lake Chad. Jul 31, 2026: Suspected militants (attribution disputed between Boko Haram and ISSP) attacked a Nigerien National Guard post and ambushed responding reinforcements. Casualty figures disputed: 14–17 killed across combined reporting.

label: Bombori (Africa Corps Massacre — 9 Civilians Killed)
sub: Mopti Region, Mali (approximate — HRW did not publish precise coordinates). Jul 10, 2026 (reported by HRW Aug 20, 2026): 100+ Africa Corps fighters raided the Fulani neighborhood of this JNIM-controlled village, killing 9 civilians including 4 children, beating dozens, and burning 8 homes.
